title: Extract Year from Hire Date
description:
Write a query to find all employees hired in the year **2020**. Return `id`, `name`, and `hire_date`.

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| hire_date | DATE |
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, hire_date DATE); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', '2020-03-15'), (2, 'Bob', '2019-07-22'), (3, 'Carol', '2021-01-10'), (4, 'Diana', '2020-11-05'), (5, 'Evan', '2018-06-30'), (6, 'Frank', '2022-09-14');
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, hire_date FROM employees WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM hire_date) = 2020

test_cases.description: Returns 2 employees hired in 2020 (Alice and Diana)

hints: `EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_column)` returns the year part as an integer you can compare with `=`.
You can also use `YEAR(hire_date)` in MySQL or `DATE_PART('year', hire_date)` in PostgreSQL.
explanation: `EXTRACT(YEAR FROM hire_date) = 2020` pulls the year from each date and keeps only rows where it equals 2020, returning Alice (hired March 2020) and Diana (hired November 2020).
